project.name: DermaScope
project.context: Browser-first facial skin signal mapping from one uploaded or captured face photo.
project.domain: Single-photo face-skin signal mapping with overlay, category scores, Skin Health Score, and zone breakdown.
project.runtimeConstraint: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI frontend with FastAPI-backed OpenCV-Python analysis.
project.architectureConstraint: Client-side SPA submits one image to /api/process and receives overlay PNG plus X-DermaScope-Analysis metadata without persistent image storage.

assumptions: DermaScope is production-facing, not coursework or a generic image-processing workbench.
The app reports visible image-processing signals and must not present diagnosis, treatment, or product recommendations.
The input flow supports file upload and browser camera capture.
The backend may be offline, so service readiness must remain visible.
Previous conservation condition-map direction is blocked by the anti-repeat ledger.

productReading.productTypeAndCoreVerb: DermaScope is a browser-first facial skin signal mapping app; the user submits one face photo and inspects mapped visible signals.
highestStakesUserMoments: Intake must make file limits, privacy, camera permission, and face-photo requirements clear before the user shares an image.
Processing must show service readiness and a non-diagnostic status while the backend analyzes the photo.
Results must connect overlay marks, category scores, and zones so users understand what the algorithm measured.
productReading.dominantDataShapes: The screen is dominated by one spatial image, five condition categories, and five face zones.
productReading.latencyProfile: Analysis is soft real-time: a single request returns a PNG overlay and metadata after processing.
productReading.failureModes: The UI must absorb offline backend, invalid image, oversized image, camera permission failure, processing failure, fallback face detection, stale result risk, and missing or malformed analysis metadata.
productReading.contextOfUse: The app is a sustained single-task inspection flow, not a feed, stored history product, or admin monitor.
productReading.knownConstraints: React + Vite + Tailwind CSS + DaisyUI are present; WCAG 2.2 AA, no persistent image storage, safe errors, and no medical diagnosis are hard constraints.

motionPaletteDecision.signatureMotionBehavior: A contour trace passes across the face result when overlay metadata arrives, then category rows and zone sectors snap into survey-station positions.
motionPaletteDecision.paletteDecision: Survey paper and hard black ink carry structure; safety orange, cyan, magenta, brown, and olive carry condition-symbol layers.
motionPaletteDecision.typographicRoleContrast: Archivo Black carries blunt survey titles, Inter carries Indonesian UI copy, and IBM Plex Mono carries station labels, scores, counts, coverage, file size, and timing.

visualResetStrategy.resetReason: The user explicitly requested a redesign with a concept that must differ from the previous direction.
discardedContinuity: archival paper and graphite/blue register palette

conceptualAnchor.name: Brutal topographic survey plate
conceptualAnchor.specificReferencePoint: Topographic maps use contour lines to show surface shape and marginal information to explain scale, symbols, and measured locations.
conceptualAnchor.rationale: The anchor supports one spatial image, condition-symbol layers, scores, and zone readings without repeating skincare, clinical, dashboard, or conservation defaults.
conceptualAnchor.signatureMove: The face photo behaves like a measured surface with marginal stations attached to condition and zone evidence.
conceptualAnchor.typographicDecision: A heavy survey-title face is paired with plain UI copy and monospaced station numerics.

typographyClusters.code: beauty-app default typography: rounded geometric sans for friendly headlines, soft medium-weight body copy, and oversized circular-score numerals.
typographyClusters.defaultReason: Consumer scan apps commonly turn analysis into coaching and progress language.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it turns evidence into lifestyle coaching.

typographyClusters.code: clinical-device default typography: restrained neo-grotesk labels, small grey metadata, and medical chart numerals in calm panels.
typographyClusters.defaultReason: Dermatology devices often borrow medical chart calm to imply authority.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it suggests diagnosis and repeats dermatology-device tropes.

typographyClusters.code: image-processing coursework typography: monospace-heavy controls, algorithm names as headings, and tiny parameter labels.
typographyClusters.defaultReason: Image-processing projects often foreground algorithms instead of user evidence.
typographyClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it foregrounds implementation instead of user evidence.

paletteClusters.code: AI skincare pastel palette: lavender/pink glow, mint secondary, cream cards, and coral concern badges.
paletteClusters.defaultReason: Consumer skin tools commonly use friendly wellness colors.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it reads as routine/product recommendation.

paletteClusters.code: clinical skin-analysis palette: white shell, mint/coral status, pale blue overlay, and low-contrast grey copy.
paletteClusters.defaultReason: Clinical-facing skin products commonly borrow clean clinic color systems.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it borrows medical-device authority.

paletteClusters.code: conservation-map palette: archival paper, graphite ink, oxidized green, vermilion, ochre, lapis, and carmine.
paletteClusters.defaultReason: The previous design used conservation condition-reporting signals.
paletteClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it is the previous blocked direction.

layoutClusters.code: beauty scan layout: selfie hero, circular score above routine cards, progress history, and product modules below.
layoutClusters.defaultReason: Skincare products commonly sell recurring coaching after the scan.
layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because DermaScope has no history or routine engine.

layoutClusters.code: clinical contact-sheet layout: before/after face panels, side metric list, small legend, and device-like header.
layoutClusters.defaultReason: Skin-analysis devices often use contact-sheet comparison and clinic controls.
layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it overstates clinical authority.

layoutClusters.code: SaaS dashboard layout: top bar, three KPI cards, neutral table, and side navigation.
layoutClusters.defaultReason: Metric-heavy apps often collapse into admin chrome.
layoutClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because a single face image is the primary evidence object.

motionClusters.code: beauty coaching motion: soft fades, sparkle reveals, and score count-up celebration.
motionClusters.defaultReason: Consumer wellness apps often use celebratory motion.
motionClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it implies improvement coaching.

motionClusters.code: clinical scanner motion: slow blue sweep, contact-sheet swap, and device-console loading bar.
motionClusters.defaultReason: Clinical imaging products often stage analysis as machine scanning.
motionClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it is too close to medical-device theater.

motionClusters.code: conservation raking-light motion: luminous sweep over artifact and register rows.
motionClusters.defaultReason: The previous design used artifact-inspection motion.
motionClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it repeats the old redesign.

imageryClusters.code: AI skincare imagery: polished selfie mockups, glowing skin overlays, and product shelf shots.
imageryClusters.defaultReason: Skincare apps often use aspirational selfie and product imagery.
imageryClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it points toward ecommerce.

imageryClusters.defaultReason: Clinical tools often use device imagery to signal precision.
imageryClusters.rejectionNote: I will not ship this because it implies a validated device.

imageryClusters.code: student demo imagery: generic before/after canvas, sample image placeholders, and algorithm screenshots.
imageryClusters.defaultReason: Coursework projects often show technical demos instead of production flows.

candidates.jobFit: Converts one face photo into a mapped surface with condition symbols, contour-like signal bands, and station rows.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: The face map is primary; score, categories, and zones become marginal station readings.
candidates.densityImplication: Compact brutal rows carry authority while preserving a large mapped surface.
candidates.typeImplication: Heavy survey title pairs with plain body and monospaced station numerics.
candidates.stateLanguage: Unmapped, acquiring, tracing, mapped, fallback, exception.
candidates.motionImplication: Contour trace reveals analysis completion; station rows snap into measured positions.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Rules out beauty coaching, clinical contact sheets, conservation registers, and generic dashboard chrome.

candidates.anchorReference: NOAA U.S. Chart No. 1 sounding and depth-contour chart
candidates.jobFit: Attaches numeric readings to a surface and separates condition layers with legend discipline.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: Surface map plus sounding labels, with legend rows carrying the score language.
candidates.densityImplication: High density is acceptable when symbols remain explained.
candidates.typeImplication: Plain chart labels pair with tabular soundings.
candidates.stateLanguage: Unsurveyed, sounded, shoal, safe contour, warning.
candidates.motionImplication: Depth contour lines resolve into category meters.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Rules out routine cards and lifestyle copy.

candidates.anchorReference: geologic field notebook strike-and-dip station log
candidates.jobFit: Supports numbered observations and zone records, but is less visually tied to the overlay.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: Station rows dominate, with the image behaving as supporting evidence.
candidates.densityImplication: Dense readings are expected, but the face could lose primacy.
candidates.typeImplication: Handbook-like headings pair with mono station coordinates.
candidates.motionImplication: Rows appear as field observations after capture.

categoryCodeOverlap.reasoning: If made mono-only it could become a technical ledger, so role contrast must stay stronger than mono labels.

candidates.jobFit: Good for layered signal fronts such as redness and texture, but risks overdramatizing skin signals.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: The image can host fronts and bands; rows explain system state.
candidates.densityImplication: Moderate density with strong symbol explanation.
candidates.typeImplication: Weather-station numerics pair with plain labels.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Rules out conservation motion and beauty celebration.

candidates.anchorReference: seismic intensity shake map with station readings
candidates.jobFit: Good for severity bands and uncertainty, but the disaster association is too severe for a personal face analysis surface.
candidates.hierarchyImplication: Intensity bands surround a central surface with station rows attached.
candidates.densityImplication: High-impact severity bands may overpower normal result states.
candidates.typeImplication: Emergency-map numerics pair with high-contrast labels.
candidates.motionImplication: Intensity bands expand from measured stations.
candidates.whatItRulesOut: Rules out soft wellness and generic dashboard rhythm.

derivedTokenLogic.colorDerivationSource: Cartographic symbol separation: paper and black ink for structure, high-chroma symbol colors only for condition layers and focus.
derivedTokenLogic.spacingDerivationSource: Map marginalia and survey station rows, with a 12px base and accessible 44px minimum target treatment.
derivedTokenLogic.typographyDerivationSource: Map title, marginal labels, and station numerics drive display/body/mono roles.
derivedTokenLogic.motionDerivationSource: Contour tracing and station snapping drive result reveal and row settlement.
derivedTokenLogic.colorSpace: sRGB CSS variables with OKLCH-safe contrast checks by visual audit where supported.
derivedTokenLogic.typeScaleMethod: Fixed role sizes with clamp only for major display labels; no viewport-width font scaling.
derivedTokenLogic.motionBudget: 150-300ms for interaction states, 420ms maximum for result contour trace, reduced-motion fallback required.
derivedTokenLogic.validationRule: Tokens must preserve WCAG 2.2 AA contrast, non-color-only condition meaning, and must not recreate the previous conservation palette.

derivationSource.typography: New roles replace Space Grotesk/IBM Plex Sans/JetBrains Mono with a survey-title/body/station system.
derivationSource.palette: New cartographic layer colors replace conservation inks.
derivationSource.spacing: Survey stations replace conservation register rows.

aiSafeUiAudit.paletteEvidence: The palette maps condition signals to cartographic symbol layers rather than mood, beauty, or clinic tone.
aiSafeUiAudit.nonTransferableBehavior: Contour and station colors attach to face-signal mapping and would not make sense in a shopping or routine product.

productionContentPolicy.language: Indonesian UI copy may be used, but formal docs stay English.

crossViewportAdaptation.mobile: Source action and service state first; face surface before register after image exists; no shrunken sidebars.
crossViewportAdaptation.tablet: Face surface wide, score and condition register below in two columns, zones as a compact station strip.
crossViewportAdaptation.desktop: Two-column survey sheet with mapped face left and evidence stations right.

motionSystem.reducedMotion: Immediate overlay replacement and static rows.

componentMorphology.radius: 0 to 4px for brutal survey surfaces; avoid soft wellness pills except compact status tags where required.
componentMorphology.shadow: Minimal; use borders, offset blocks, and surface contrast instead of soft card depth.

designExecutionPolicy.reason: Native CSS can deliver the selected contour trace, station snap, and responsive recomposition without adding runtime surface.
designExecutionPolicy.oldDesignRegressionTest: Reject if the result preserves the conservation artifact/register composition, raking-light motion, or archival palette.

designExecutionHandoff.implementationMove: Use strong sheet borders, station rows, and contour trace as functional result affordances.

zone and category data are readable at a glance

repoEvidence.designEvidenceSummary: The repo contains a React + Vite frontend, FastAPI processing backend, one DermaScope goal, camera/upload intake, overlay PNG output, category scores, and zone breakdown docs. Legacy ImgLab static files and generic operation contracts are cleanup targets.
